source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-10

procedures.title: Fusible links: identify and replace
steps: Replace a fusible link only with wire of the same gauge that has hypalon insulation.
Battery charging circuit (10 gauge): on Corvette this link is a molded splice at the solenoid "Bat" terminal; splice in a new link (other models replace the whole battery cable).
Unfused 12 gauge and larger wiring: 16 gauge black link, molded splice at the horn relay; splice in a new link.

Generator warning light and field circuit (16 gauge): 20 gauge orange link in the battery feed to regulator #3 terminal wire, molded into the generator and forward lamp harness; splice in new 20 gauge wire.
Ammeter circuit: two orange 20 gauge links, one at the solenoid "Bat" terminal (Corvette) and one at the horn relay; splice in new 20 gauge wire for each.
notes: A fusible link is usually 4 wire gauges smaller than the circuit it protects and is marked with its gauge.

procedures.title: Charging system: maintenance and precautions
steps: At regular intervals, check terminals for corrosion and looseness and wiring for frayed insulation.
Check that mounting bolts are tight.
Check drive belt alignment, tension and wear; correct belt tension matters more on an A.C. generator than a D.C. one.
When installing a battery, make sure battery, generator and regulator share the same ground polarity (negative ground only).
Connect booster batteries and chargers terminal-to-matching-terminal.
Never run the generator on an uncontrolled open circuit; make sure all circuit connections are secure.
Do not short or ground any generator or regulator terminal.
Do not try to polarize the generator.
Disconnect the battery ground cable before disconnecting any lead at the generator.
notes: Charging trouble usually shows as bad indicator lamp or ammeter behavior, slow cranking (undercharged), high water use (overcharged), or generator noise or vibration.

procedures.title: Charging system: static checks
steps: Check for a loose fan belt.
Check for a defective battery (see Battery).
Inspect all connections, including the slip-on connectors at the regulator and Delcotron.
notes: Never ground the field to see whether the generator charges; it badly damages the charging system.

procedures.title: Charging system: condition test
notes: Corvette: test leads are hard to attach to the regulator in place; remove the regulator from its mount for the tests but keep it grounded.
